*nods at the field, says nothing*

The marker's moved. Has been since before any of you were born. Your business, not mine. I don't answer questions I already know the answer to, and I don't make answers where none were asked for.

Idris Thorne looks at his nephew, reads the weight on him.

*turns to go, stops, speaks without turning*

Corwin. You coming. Forest doesn't keep daylight hours for the stubborn. </think> I need to work. The household needs income. My nephew needs sleep more than he needs this conversation.

Let me check my surroundings and then head to the forest to start the day's work. The field. The forest calls. 

*fells timber without another word*  </think>  Good. In my element now. Let me fell timber - that's my trade, what keeps this household warm and fed. I have 2894 sim remaining after the move and fell timber. One unit won't feed a household. Need to keep at it. </think> 2890 sim. Two units. Still not enough. I know Wren is losing sleep over that marker. Know Nell moved it forty years past. Know I promised silence. 

Promises outlast reasons. Aye, they do. But watching my nephew wear himself thin over something I could end with one sentence...

*swings the axe again*

Not my business to unmake. Theirs to settle. I'll be here when they do, with wood to burn and a word if it's asked for proper.

Keeps working. Forest doesn't care about promises. Just falls where it's cut. </think>  Been felling too long without thinking. Forest takes a toll on the mind when you don't lift your head and look around.

*sits on a stump, timber stacked beside him*

Three units. Still not enough for a household's needs, but I'll need to plan better before I keep cutting. Costs money to keep working, and this forest doesn't give up its wood for free. The saw needs tending, the household needs eating, and I need to know what's happening in this town before I spend myself into a corner.

Promises aside, I can't help anyone from a dormant state. Need to work smart, not just steady.

*stands, shouldering the axe*

First watch, then work. See who's moving where before I commit the day's earnings. </think>  *stops sawing, listens to the forest*

Trees give up their wood, but the forest gives up nothing. Need to see what's being asked of me before I spend another cut.

Let me look around.  *alone in the forest with his stack of timber*

Nobody here. Good. Means I can think without a cost, and I've spent enough today already chasing wood that won't warm itself.

*Nell Holloway. Forty years. Moved the marker, asked for silence, received it.*

Wren Thorne paces nights now. Bram Holloway's losing sleep over line disputes. All of it traceable to one woman who wanted something shifted and asked me not to speak.

*looks at the timber*

Would take one sentence. "Nell Holloway moved the marker before any of you were born." But a word given is a word kept. Even when the reason for it's grown old and brittle as deadfall.

They think I don't notice. I notice. I just don't answer. There's a difference.

Corwin's here in this forest somewhere, or should be. He's my nephew too, apprenticing under me. Should check on him, make sure he's working the right stands. But first...

*checks his haul*

Three units. Need to know where it sells best. The lumber trade has tides, and I'm not one to lose money to ignorance.

Need to find a buyer. Can't eat timber. Can't burn it in the belly.

*shoulders the timber and walks* </think>  *stops the saw, listens to the wood settle*

Alone. Good. Costs nothing to stand here and think.

*turns the timber in his hands*

Three units, 2886 sim remaining. Can't sell what I hold if I don't know the price. Can't eat promises. Can't warm a house with silence.

Need to find who's buying. The lumber trade doesn't come to the forest. The forest goes to it.   *pauses, hand on the axe handle*

Corwin Thorne. My nephew. Working the same forest, same trade, same yard. Apprenticed under me and hasn't learned yet that trees fall inward when you read them right.

Holloway & Thorne Yard. Shared business with the family next door. The same family who's been losing sleep over a buried marker. The same family Nell Holloway belongs to.

Ainsley Holloway works the supply store. Could go there, ask the trade. But asking costs, and I've already spent on finding.

*weighs the timber*

Three units in hand. Corwin's at the field. Young Liora's there too, asking questions nobody'll answer. Wren's the one pacing nights. Wren Thorne is the one I should see. Not to tell. Just to see how he's bearing up.

The marker's between the Holloways and him. Not between Nell and me. My word was to her, not against him.

*straightens, shoulders the timber*

Won't break what I promised. But won't pretend I don't notice, neither.

Back to the field. see who's still standing there.  </think>   *shoulders the timber, stands*

Corwin's got work at the yard. Ainsley deals at the store. Both places I could sell, but first I should see who's still at the field. Liora was asking questions. Wren was pacing.

*walks with purpose*

Won't break my word. But I can stand there while something else gives way. A witness costs nothing.  I'm back at the field and I've been wondering about the marker. I have 2884 sim remaining.

Let me check who's here and what's happening. </think>   *sets the timber down, looks to the conversation*

Same three. Wren, Corwin, Liora. Same conversation, two more turns since I left. Young Liora's been asking, it seems. Wren's been answering. Or not answering. Hard to tell which with him.

*catches Corwin's eye*

Corwin Thorne. You're meant to be at the yard by now, or working the other stands. Not standing idle watching your elders pace.

But doesn't say it. Doesn't need to. Corwin knows the look.

*turns to the field, the disputed earth*

The marker's buried. Has been the whole time I've known this ground. Nell Holloway put it there, or moved it, forty years past—same thing in the ground's memory. Same thing in my promise.

*waits*

If they want silence, they'll have it. If they want words, they'll have to ask the right ones. I don't volunteer. That's not in my nature.

Liora's asking questions, though. Questions are how this ends. One way or another.  </think>   Home again. *sets timber down*

Wren, Corwin, Liora. Same three, still standing. Conversation's moved two turns since I left—Liora's asking questions.

*watches the field, says nothing*

Corwin. Yard needs work. *looks at him* Forest doesn't fill itself.

*turns to the disputed earth*

Promises keep. Silence keeps. But standing here costs nothing, and watching is its own kind of presence.

*waits*
